svg.title: Handling a Nonstationary VAR
svg.desc: The path from unit root tests through the Johansen rank test to a level VAR, a VECM or a differenced VAR, with the pitfalls at each step.
svg.text: The procedure for a nonstationary VAR
Unit roots → lags and deterministic terms → Johansen rank → model branch → diagnostics → interpretation
1. Multivariate series in levels y(t)
2. Unit root test on each series
ADF · PP · KPSS — on levels and first differences
3. Confirm the order of integration I(1)
Is it stationary after differencing, and is the order the same across series?
4. Set lag p and deterministic terms
AIC·BIC·HQ, and decide on constant and trend
5. Johansen rank test
Set r with trace and max-eigenvalue tests
Differenced VAR
No cointegration — estimate on Δy
0 < r < n
VECM
Includes the error-correction term, keeping the long-run relation
r = n
Level VAR
Already stationary — keep the levels
6. Diagnostics
Residual autocorrelation (LM), normality, stability (roots inside the unit circle), breaks (CUSUM)
7. Interpretation and outputs
IRF, FEVD, Granger causality, forecasts and scenarios
Pitfall · low power
Unit root tests have low power.
Read ADF and KPSS together,
a structural break can flip the conclusion.
Pitfall · setting sensitivity
The choice of lags and deterministic terms
changes the outcome of the rank test.
Check under alternative settings.
Pitfall · wrong branch
Differencing a cointegrated system
loses the long-run information,
using a VECM when there is none
a spurious correction term appears.
Pitfall · after-the-fact checks
If autocorrelation remains in the residuals, add lags.
Eigenvalues outside the unit circle mean instability —
do not take the interpretation at face value.
Summary
You do not decide on differencing first — estimate the rank r, and the model follows.
Each decision changes the next step, so re-checking under different settings is essential.
Branching rule
(the rank picks the model)
For a VECM the equation is Δy(t) = αβ′y(t−1) + ΣΓΔy(t−i) + ε(t)
Read with Differenced VAR vs VECM and Engle-Granger vs Johansen for the whole procedure.
